title: Output Scan Loop
statement: Let $C$ be a family of Boolean circuits, and fix Boolean $\ell_m$ and natural numbers $n,i,B$. For every $V\le B$, if $W+d=V$, $k\le i$, $U\le B$, and $k+d+1\le B$, then the walk initialized in state $oL$ with registers $(k,V,U,W)$ and no result has the following behavior on the input encoding $n$ and $i$: if $k\le i<k+d+1$, it halts with answer $\ell_m$ or the $(i-k)$-th bit of the word consisting of $d$ ones followed by zero; if $k+d+1\le i$, it reaches the specified postcondition, with registers $(k+d+1,V,U,V)$ and state $done$, while all registers are bounded by $B$ throughout the run before reaching it.
